Industrialisation et fabrication de munitions navales téléopérées et prestations associées (phase candidature).
Les conflits actuels démontrent que les drones et les systèmes autonomes sont devenus des capacités déterminantes, évoluant à un rythme sans précédent. C’est pourquoi la DGA a pour objectif de transformer plus rapidement les innovations en capacités opérationnelles au profit des Forces. Ainsi, le Centre Expert Référent Drones et systèmes Autonomes Navals (CERDAN) a pour mission de piloter le passage à l’échelle depuis le prototypage étatique à une série déployable sur les bâtiments de la Marine Nationale. Dans ce contexte et dans le cadre du projet interne SMOKERS, les centres techniques de la DGA conçoivent rapidement des solutions au plus près du terrain et des besoins opérationnels. Leurs équipes ont conçu et testé des prototypes de drones navals munitions téléopérées (MNTO), et souhaitent confier à un industriel l’ajustement de la conception, la production d’un dossier de fabrication, la mise en place de l’outil industriel de production et une production à un rythme répondant aux besoins des forces en MNTO. Il est envisagé des séries d’environ 10 / an en temps de paix et une capacité de 50 drones par an en fonction de l’évolution du contexte géopolitique. La présente procédure répond au besoin d’externaliser l’industrialisation, la fabrication et la gestion de configurations de ces MNTO à partir du dossier de conception du prototype V1 fourni par la DGA. Les caractéristiques techniques actuelles d’une MNTO SMOKERS V1 sont : - Poids 500 kg ; dimension 5 m de long ; - Moyen SatCom, RF et caméra IR ; système embarqué - Autonomie > à 50 nautiques, et vitesse max 40 nœuds.

normalized.description: Objective:To design and realize a first European portable self-calibrated SI-traceable Rydberg atom-based Electric field probe.Description:Accurate measurement of electric fields is crucial for the development and operation of RF communicationsystems, particularly in space missions. Conventional antennas need fine calibration for high-integrity reception. The calibration is performed by placing uncalibrated antennas in a known EM (electromagnetic) environment that is measured via a well-calibrated antenna which creates a dependency. Whereas Rydberg based receivers allow precise measurements of RF signals which is directly related to Planck's constant and hence can self-calibrate by relying on SI (international system of units)-traceable atomic standards The activity aims to develop a portable, self-calibrated Rydberg atom based electric field probe.The probe is based on the interaction of RF-fields with Rydberg atoms, where alkali atoms are excited opticallyto Rydberg states and the applied RF-field alters the resonant state of the atoms. For this probe, the Rydbergatoms are placed in a glass vapor cell. The vapor cell acts like an RF-to-optical transducer, converting an RF Efield to an optical frequency response. The probe utilizes the concept of Electromagnetic Induced Transition (EIT), where the RF transition in the four-level atomic system causes a split of the transition spectrum for the pump laser. This splitting is measured and is directly proportional to the applied RF field amplitude. Therefore, by measuring this splitting, we get a direct measurement of the RF E-field strength. This technique could allow traceable measurements over a large frequency band including 1-500GHz. The new approach has the following benefits: 1) it will allow direct SI units linked RF E-field measurements, 2) It is self-calibrating due to atomic resonances, 3) it will provide RF field measurements independent of current techniques, 4) the probe will not perturb the field during the measurement, since no metal is present in the probe.This activity encompasses the following tasks:-Assessment of different Rydberg atom-based methods of detection of RF fields.- Requirement consolidation and performance assessment.- Detailed concept design with analysis of critical functions.- Development of the breadboard and verification in relevant environment.- Development of a technology roadmap for an EQM.

normalized.title: S3-CL-05 SIMPLIFIED LCA AND ECODESIGN TOOL FOR SPACE MISSIONS - EXPRO+
normalized.description: Following the endorsement of the ESA Ecodesign Policy in October 2025, the systematic integration of ecodesign principles into ESA programmes and projects has become a key enabler for achieving ESA Green Agenda objectives. However, current Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approaches remain too complex and resource-intensive for routine use during mission conception and preliminary design. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a simplified LCA and ecodesign tool for space missions, enabling rapid environmental assessments and the comparison of alternative design solutions during phases A/B1. The tool developed in this activity will provide a practical and harmonised means to support ecodesign implementation across the European space sector while ensuring consistency with ESA environmental datasets and European assessment methodologies. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 6.

normalized.title: EO4SLOVENIA - AN EO BASED SOLUTION FOR NATURAL HAZARDS AND WATER RESOURCES IN SLOVENIA - EXPRO+
normalized.description: Water Resources Management (WRM) and Disaster Risk Management (DRM) are two thematic areas that are important in Slovenia. In 2025 a preparatory activity concerning the contribution of satellite data for different thematic areas has highlighted the needs of priorities of a group of nationally mandated stakeholders from both the WRM sector and the DRM sector. While the ESA Digital Twin Earth (ESA DTE) programme is looking at integrating Earth Observation (EO) satellite capabilities in future operational Digital Twins ecosystems, including the potential future evolution of DestinE and other operational DT initiatives in Europe, this activity is a precursor development under the FutureEO programme to prepare the ground for an EO based digital ecosystem and connect EO data, processingchains and modelling. This FutureEO activity aims to implement and demonstrate a preliminary Digital Twin Precursor to prefigure potential EO based Digital Twin developments. This ITT refers to implementing an EO-based Digital Twin precursor for the themes Water Resources Management and Disaster Risk Management for Slovenia identified through community consultation and considered to be mature enough to start a large activity. For both WRM and DRM themes, the project shall deliver end-to-end pre-operational solutions, fullyimplemented, conceptually and technically mature, scientifically validated, and fully tested by a representative set of early adopters.

normalized.title: MULTI-BAND DUAL-BEAM C-TO-Q/V SATCOM ANALOGUE BEAMFORMING INTEGRATED CIRCUIT (ARTES AT 7B.091) - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
normalized.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a wideband analogue beamforming integrated circuit (BFIC) capable of covering the entire frequency range from Cto Q/V-band, with two beams. This BFIC will serve as a modular and scalable solution for user-terminal flat-panel arrays, enabling multi-band and multi-product compatibility.Targeted Improvements: - Frequency coverage extended from C-band to Q/V-band in a single BFIC.- Fostering high-volume production scalability and economies of scale.- Enhanced design modularity, enabling flat-panel antennas to scale in aperture size (same number of beams) and/or number of beams (same aperture).Description:Conventionally, different BFICs have been used in applications at different frequency bands, e.g., the C- to Q/V-bands relevant to satcom. Also, such conventional BFICs typically generate a single beam. To enable the use of thesame BFIC in a broad range of satcom products, this activity will develop a next-generation dual-beam analogue BFIC with wideband coverage from C- to Q/V-band. Thus, the envisioned BFIC will serve as a fundamental building block for future flat-panel antenna arrays, supporting scalable designs by allowing additional BFICs to be integrated based on performance requirements. The development of this BFIC shall leverage insights from recent state-of-the-art wideband single-/dual-beam BFICs, such as the C- to Ka-band BFICs, which are developed outside ESA Member States. These contributions highlight the growing industry demand for multi-beam and frequency-agnostic BFIC solutions, which can reduce system complexity and accelerate product development, with the potential for higher volumeproduction in comparison to single-band BFICs. Therefore, the envisioned BFIC will cover the entire C- to Q/V-band range and generatetwo beams, which will enable its reuse across multiple product lines and reduce the need for band-specific BFICs. The design willemphasise performance consistency across the wide frequency range, minimising variations in gain, noise figure, and linearity.Additionally, the activity will assess the thermal and power consumption challenges associated with multi-beam and broadband analogue BFICs at millimetre-wave frequencies, ensuring that the proposed solution is viable for both low- and high-end satcom applications. Successful execution will position Europe as a leader in wideband BFICs, securing our competitiveness in the evolving satcom ecosystem. The wideband analogue BFIC will be tested against DVB-S2/S2X or 5G-NR waveform in a relevant environment.

normalized.description: ESA operates one of the world's largest Earth Observation (EO) data archives, with data from missions dating back to the mid 1970s.Preserving these datatogether with the information and tools needed to interpret and use themis essential to analyse long-term environmental changes and support future decision-making. Within the EOF-EOS framework, long-term preservation of ESA's EO data holdings (Heritage Missions, Earth Explorers, Third Party Missions) and associated information and software is ensured through the Space Data Preservation System (SDPS), with assets located at ESRIN and external sites.Despite major progress, a significant volume of EO heritage data remains stored on legacy media at ESRIN and still requires transcription, recovery, and preservation in line with international standards. Beyond preservation and access, heritage data must be curated and improved to ensure continuity and comparability with newer missions. The generation of thematic collections and geographical datasets has further enhanced their usability and value.The Preservation Assets Operations and Maintenance (PAOM) Service will:Operate, maintain, and evolve Space Data Preservation System (SDPS) assets located at ESRIN;Manage the ESRIN EO Legacy Media Archive and Transcription Chains and perform legacy media transcription and data recovery;Generate thematic collections and geographical coverages using heritage data;Manage the ESRIN laboratory activities in support to transcription chains set-up and Philab Air Quality Platform activities, and manage and maintain the ESRIN AF Antenna;Support local visits at the Heritage Missions Walkthrough and Memorabilia Wall located at ESRIN and heritage missionsrelated outreach activities.
